summary: Revision 3 retains all 88 stable nodes, 19 planets and the independent revision-2 review object. It repairs R2 with unrestricted ambient module-sheaf pullback, sheaf tensors, stalkwise quasi-nilpotence and a common crystal/de Rham/Poincaré adapter; R4 with the actual W[t] degree-zero lift, relative SNC zero divisor, divisor log and compatible induced higher system; and R5 with completed finite locally free crystal systems, explicit p-inversion, compatible specified algebraization and locally split transverse sheaf filtrations. Fine/fs and bounded-below support corrections are retained. Four inherited source gaps and nine single-owner requests remain. All four stages are planned, none is closed, and all implementations remain unchecked.

nodes.statement: A prelog ring is a commutative ring A, a commutative monoid P and a homomorphism α:P→(A,×), including elements mapping to zero. A morphism consists of a ring map and a monoid map commuting with α. Additive notation for charts corresponds to multiplication in A.
proofSteps: Use the multiplicative monoid of the ring, not its unit group.
Define morphisms by the commuting square and componentwise composition.
acceptance: The standard chart ℕ→A sends n to tⁿ, including t=0.

For the converse obtain local charts and separate the free cokernel directions; apply the ordinary étale or smooth lifting criterion.

On the source quasi-étale tube site define f_!F=ker(F→g_*g*F), with the exactness properties in DL Definition B.1. Apply Ru_*Rs_* to the supported de Rham complex to define ω_(U,X) and ω̃_(U,X). This is analytic-tube support. There is a natural map from special-fiber F_!F*Rs_* to Rs_*f_!, which need not be a categorical factorization or an isomorphism in general.
proofSteps: Use the exact support kernel on the quasi-étale analytic tube site supplied by RD.4.
Apply the support functor before the analytic specialization pushforward and then the embedding-system pushforward.
Construct the special-fiber comparison by the adjunction map and preserve its direction.
acceptance: For U=X the support kernel is the identity.

Thus Nφ=pφN in the same convention as the crystalline embedding model. Apply the source exact support functor on tubes before taking derived pushforwards.
proofSteps: Take the absolute-relative log differential short exact sequence on the embedding tube.
Apply the exact tube support functor and derived specialization/hypercover pushforward.
Identify the connecting map with the fixed N convention and Frobenius scaling.

nodes.title: Sato logarithmic residue variant
nodes.statement: For a strictly semistable X/k^log, use an admissible embedding system over W(k)[t]^log with source a strict Zariski hypercover of X. Its degree-zero lift Z⁰ is flat and generically smooth over W[t], smooth over W, and the actual fibre Y⁰=(t=0) is a relative strict normal crossings divisor over W. Its log structure is the divisor log of Y⁰, and its special fibre is formed by the actual structure map and k^log→W[t]^log. Higher levels are the compatible Grosse-Klönne induced system. On each lift define Ω_+^q as the sheaf cokernel of ordinary absolute (q+1)-forms into absolute log (q+1)-forms over W; restrict to the prescribed fibre, realize on the tube and totalize. Derived specialization gives ω_X^+, naturally comparable with WΞ_X⊗ℚ. For support along U, apply the analytic tube support functor before specialization in this same system; retain the natural special-fibre-support comparison without declaring it invertible. CR.4 owns WΞ and its ordered residue sequence. The q+1 shift, stratum ordering and coefficient-module convention are essential.
proofSteps: Choose the source strict Zariski hypercover and the degree-zero W[t] lift satisfying flatness, generic smoothness over Frac(W[t]), W-smoothness and the actual relative SNC zero-divisor condition. Identify the log structure with that divisor log and the special fibre by pullback along the prescribed log point.

Use Grosse-Klönne §§5.1–5.2: form products of degree-zero lifts over W, blow up the corresponding products of flat divisor components, remove strict transforms, and take the exceptional divisor with the diagonal embeddings. Retain all face, degeneracy, augmentation and structure-map compatibilities.

Form the sheaf cokernel of ordinary-to-log absolute forms in degree q+1 on these actual lifts. Restrict to the zero fibre and use the RD Part II completion/tube realization and totalization tied to the same embedding system.
Apply Sato Definition 8.3 and Propositions 8.4 and 8.6, pp.211–213, to compare the ordered-stratum residue complexes with rational WΞ. Transport its module structure.

For U⊂X use the same embedding’s exact tube support kernel before derived specialization. Construct the map from special-fibre extension by zero to that supported residue complex; DL does not identify these two support procedures.
acceptance: For a smooth component the homological Witt sheaf agrees with ordinary WΩ; on a crossing the ordering controls the higher residue signs.

nodes.statement: For a proper strictly semistable special log fiber Y over a perfect field, the log rigid HK complex over W(k)[1/p] supplied by RD.4 is canonically comparable with the rational log crystalline HK complex, compatibly with φ, N and the uniformizer-dependent de Rham comparison. proofSteps: Use the proper convergent/crystalline comparison for log smooth embedding systems.
Compare the log rigid boundary-complex models with the same log parameter specializations and their θ triangles.
Use proper de Rham/dagger comparison to match the uniformizer maps.
acceptance: In good reduction it agrees with the ordinary proper rigid–crystalline comparison.

nodes.title: Ramified Hyodo–Kato base change
nodes.statement: For a finite residue extension k′/k and log base k′^(d)→k^log given by ℕ→ℕ, 1↦d, d≥1, put N^(d)=N_raw/d on the HK complex of a model over k′^(d). For a base change Y′=Y×_{k^log}k′^(d), the rational comparison C_HK^(d)(Y′)≃C_HK(Y)⊗_{K₀}W(k′)[1/p] is (φ,N)-equivariant with this normalized N^(d). Without normalization raw monodromy scales by d. In characteristic p, this is not a claim that the d=p root map is log étale.
proofSteps: Compare the standard log-base parameter under t↦t^d, so dlog t becomes d dlog t′.
Use rational log crystalline/log rigid base change in the semistable setting and divide the raw boundary by d.
Transport Frobenius and verify the normalized connecting diagram.
acceptance: For d=1 it is unramified base change; for d>1 omitting the 1/d changes the monodromy diagram.

nodes.title: Hyodo–Kato cohomology of Stein curves
nodes.statement: For a smooth semistable Stein curve with a semistable weak formal model and a Stein exhaustion by relatively compact dagger/semistable pieces U_i, define its overconvergent HK cohomology using the RD.4 log rigid complex and its continuous projective-limit cohomology interface. H¹_HK is a projective limit of finite-dimensional K₀-spaces, with its Fréchet topology and continuous φ,N. The required strictness and limit hypotheses belong to the analytic owner. This is not ordinary nonproper crystalline cohomology.
proofSteps: Import the semistable weak formal and dagger exhaustion with the specified restriction maps.
Take the log rigid cohomology and use strict differential and inverse-limit results to identify it with the projective limit of finite-dimensional groups.
Endow it with the limit topology and continuous operators rather than a bare vector-space limit.
acceptance: The Stein curve model gives a separated Fréchet HK space; arbitrary affinoid classical HK need not share this property.

The representation classification of the tower belongs to its automorphic owner. proofSteps: Apply the nonproper curve HK construction at each finite level with the source semistable models.
Use the transition maps and form the ind-Fréchet colimit retaining its actions.

nodes.title: Finite projective coefficient interfaces
nodes.statement: Import a finite locally free ordinary crystal from CR.1 or log crystal from CR.5. At every PD object T export its actual finite locally free module sheaf F_T and coherent sheaf-pullback isomorphisms. Only on affine T identify its sections with a finite projective Γ(T,O_T)-module. A log PD-smooth embedding gives the integrable stalkwise quasi-nilpotent sheaf connection using the common crystal evaluation. Tensor, internal dual and End preserve these evaluation maps. Completed coefficients are compatible finite locally free crystals at all W/p^(n+1) levels, with compatible reductions and morphisms; on an O-model use the canonical PD thickenings M/p⊂M/p^(n+1). Rational coefficients retain an integral system and invert p on morphisms, giving K₀-linear Hom spaces.
proofSteps: Reuse the CR.1/CR.5 module-sheaf crystal category and add finite local freeness on every ambient evaluation. The affine QC equivalence then gives finite projective section modules.
Use the same ambient sheaf evaluation and canonical transition maps for tensor, dual and the PD connection; do not replace nonaffine sheaves by global modules.

Form compatible crystal systems over the trivial-log Witt PD bases W/p^(n+1), with source M/p and the canonical PD(p) model evaluations. Require adjacent reduction isomorphisms and their morphism squares; compose them for all reductions.

Retain the integral system as an object presentation and localize Hom by K₀⊗_W Hom, extending composition bilinearly. Evaluation on the actual model PD thickenings retains the same reduction isomorphisms before rationalization.
acceptance: The rank-one structure crystal evaluates to O_T with d and its base extension map.

nodes.title: Filtered arithmetic coefficient interfaces
nodes.statement: On a semistable O-model M, a rational coefficient is a compatible completed finite locally free crystal system over W/p^(n+1), with source M/p, followed by explicit p-inversion. Geometric Frobenius pullback is levelwise crystalline pullback along absolute Frobenius of M/p and Witt σ; require an invertible horizontal linearization φ:σ*C→C when used. A monodromy map N:C→C is a crystal morphism with Nφ=pφσ*N. To specify a de Rham sheaf on the full algebraic generic fibre, supply a finite locally free integrable O_M/W connection lattice whose reductions are horizontally and coherently identified with these very model PD evaluations. This algebraization is additional data; formal completion alone does not supply it on an arbitrary nonproper M. Restrict that lattice to M_K and pass to K-relative forms. Give this sheaf an exhaustive separated decreasing filtration by étale-locally split sheaf submodules, with ∇Fil^i contained in the sheaf image of Fil^(i−1)⊗Ω¹. Compatible model pullback retains level reductions, commutes with Frobenius, and pulls back this realized filtration and connection. Twist C(r) scales φ by p^(−r), retains N and shifts Fil^i to Fil^(i+r). R06.2 supplies these normalization conventions, not the geometric crystal category.
proofSteps: Use the completed finite locally free systems and localized Hom category from finite-projective-coefficients. Construct levelwise model and Frobenius pullback, with natural comparison isomorphisms commuting with level reduction and Witt-semilinear scalars.

Evaluate C_n on the actual M/p⊂M/p^(n+1) PD thickenings. Specify a finite locally free integrable algebraic lattice and horizontal reduction isomorphisms commuting with adjacent ambient reduction; this is an algebraization of the same formal evaluation, not a universal algebraization theorem.

Pull that lattice back to the actual generic fibre and quotient W-relative forms to K-relative forms. Define filtration subobjects using the native module-sheaf submodule lattice, with complements only after étale localization. Express Griffiths transversality in the sheaf tensor image.

Pull back the integral systems, realized connection and locally split filtration along a compatible model morphism. Check the Frobenius commutation square, monodromy conjugation and sheaf filtration transport on that same evaluation.
Apply the R06.2 period convention φ_r=p^(−r)φ and Fil^i_r=Fil^(i+r); scalars preserve invertibility and the Nφ relation.
acceptance: The Tate twist convention agrees with R06.2 and the standard R07.2 modules.

nodes.title: Dieudonné variance and Tate twists
nodes.statement: Over perfect k, the evaluated contravariant crystal agrees with the exact R07.2 modules: D(Q_p/Z_p)=W(k)e with Fe=e, Ve=pe (semilinearity understood), and D(μ_{p∞})=W(k)e with Fe=pe, Ve=e. Rationally the latter is K₀(−1) under φ_{D(r)}=p^{−r}φ_D, while the constant group gives K₀(0). Cartier duality agrees with D(G∨)≅D(G)∨(−1). Verify the horizontal evaluation maps and variance, not only the slopes.
proofSteps: Evaluate the existing crystalline functor at the Witt PD thickening and compare to the standard modules already owned by R07.2.
Check Frobenius/Verschiebung and the contravariant group-map direction.
Apply Cartier duality and the declared twist convention to identify the rank-one rational modules.

nodes.title: Grothendieck–Messing filtration interfaces
nodes.statement: For a nilpotent PD thickening S₀→S with p locally nilpotent and the nilpotent divided powers required by R07.2, export the actual evaluation D(G₀)_S. A chosen lift G/S of G₀ determines a locally direct summand Hodge filtration in this evaluation, reducing to the contravariant exact sequence 0→ω_{G₀}→D(G₀)_{S₀}→Lie(G₀∨)→0. The R07.2 Grothendieck–Messing equivalence identifies lifts of G₀ with lifts of this filtration. This node exports its evaluated maps and compatibility; the classification is imported, with its nilpotent-PD hypotheses.
proofSteps: Import the source-qualified R07.2 deformation theorem and its exact nilpotent-PD hypotheses.
Transport the evaluation and Hodge inclusion through the coefficient interface.
Verify base-change and duality compatibility of the actual inclusion and quotient maps.
acceptance: For the constant group the Hodge submodule is zero; for the multiplicative group it is the full rank-one evaluation.

nodes.title: Relative Gauss–Manin connections
nodes.statement: Let f:X→Y be proper smooth over a smooth base Y/S and F a finite locally free crystal with integrable quasi-nilpotent connection. Assume the relative coefficient de Rham derived image is perfect, every H^i in the degrees used is finite locally free, and the cohomology base-change maps in those degrees are isomorphisms (for instance, impose the appropriate neighboring torsion-vanishing or locally constant rank conditions supplied by CR.3). Then the derived crystalline cartesian structure induces an integrable quasi-nilpotent Gauss–Manin connection on H^i. Its map is the boundary of the first-step base-form filtration on the absolute coefficient de Rham complex.
proofSteps: Use the derived crystal evaluation over the base PD diagonal.
Under the explicit finite locally free/cohomology base-change assumptions, extract the H^i cartesian module and differentiate its PD stratification.
Identify the connection with the boundary map from the base-form filtration and prove integrability by the PD cocycle.
